title: My therapist texts: Call back or she dies?

parts: [[9:41 PM · APARTMENT]] My therapist just texted: "Call me back in five minutes or she dies." My pulse spikes. The digital clock blinks 02:00. I grip the phone, hallway stench of stale pizza and rain pounding the windows. [[3 MINUTES LEFT]] I stare at the screen. Who is "she"? Dr. Lila never threatens anyone. The vibration hums like a bomb tick. [[RULE 1 · TRUST NO ONE]] I dial the office. Click. A strained voice whispers, "She’s in the basement, tied up. Give us the address you gave last week." My breath freezes. The address—my old apartment, the one that burned. I see the shattered window, the blackened floorboards flash. [[FLASHBACK · FIRE NIGHT]] My phone buzzes again. New text: "Don’t go. She’ll die if you move." I smash the screen shut. The hallway light flickers, a low thud echoes from the stairs. My mind races. I need a plan, but the clock is merciless. I sprint toward the stairwell, heart hammering. The basement door creaks, cold air slashing my cheek. I step into darkness, the air thick with ash. A muffled scream cuts through the silence. The timer flashes 00:01. I grip the railing, the metal icy under my palm. The darkness swallows me just as the countdown hits zero—

The clock ticks, I’ve got one minute left.

The basement reeks of mildew. My flashlight sputters, shadows lurch. Muffled sobs echo behind a rusted door. [[9:58 PM · BASEMENT]] I press my ear to the cold metal. A woman's voice croaks, "Help me…" My heart hammers.

I yank the door open. No victim—just a wooden box, lid half‑gone. Inside, a crumpled note. The ink bleeds: 47 Willow Lane. My stomach knots. Dr. Lila’s text was a trap. Why?

Footsteps thunder above, shoes squealing on slick concrete. [[RULE 2 · ESCAPE]] I snatch the note, sprint toward the stairs. Water sloshes, soaking my boots. A voice roars from the hallway, "You! Stop!" I freeze. The flashlight slips, flaring a crimson burst.

In that flash, a silhouette looms—hood up, mask hiding everything. The figure freezes, then darts down the corridor, disappearing.

My mind spins. Kidnapper? Rescue? A faint click— the basement door slams shut, locking behind me. My phone blinks: ONE MINUTE LEFT.

I stare at the note, at the dripping walls, at the darkness swallowing the stairs. I can call Dr. Lila back and walk into whatever she’s set, or I can bolt for Willow Lane and maybe save someone.

The seconds melt. I lift my hand to dial, the other gripping the note tighter. A sudden bang reverberates from the hallway, the sound of a lock being turned. 

What’s waiting at Willow Lane? What’s behind that locked door?

The timer’s at zero, the girl’s fate hangs on my next move.

I’m still in the basement, heart pounding, water lapping at my shoes. I punch Dr. Lila’s number. The line clicks. A cold voice whispers, “You called. Good. She’s safe—for now.”

My breath catches. A hollow laugh cracks the silence. “You think I’m the therapist? I’m her sister. I kidnapped her to force you to the exact spot where I buried my brother.”

The phone crackles. Sirens wail in the distance, growing louder. [[RULE 3 · REVEAL]]

My lungs burn. The paper I clutched was a false trail. The real address glows in my mind: Willow Lane, the house I fled as a child.

I slam the handset. The timer blinks red—00:00. Lights sputter, then plunge the basement into darkness. A scream shreds the air. The woman I thought was a victim lunges, knife gleaming.

I dive. Metal clangs against concrete. I scramble up the stairs, water now a raging torrent, each step a roar.

I burst onto the street, rain slashing my face, and sprint toward Willow Lane, the address burning in my head. I fling the front door open, gasping for air.

Inside, a small room bathes in red light. In the center, a child is tied, eyes wide with terror. Dr. Lila’s sister steps forward, gun leveled, a cruel smile curling her lips.

“Too late,” she hisses.

I raise my hands. The gun clicks. The scene freezes.

Was calling back a trap that saved a child or doomed more? So… was I right to trust a therapist who was really the kidnapper’s sister?

premise.hook: My therapist just texted me: "If you don't call me back in 5 minutes, she'll die."
premise.twist: The therapist is actually the kidnapper’s sister, using the narrator to locate the hidden victim.
premise.debate: Viewers will argue whether the narrator should trust a professional who’s apparently complicit, or if calling back is a trap that endangers more people.
